analyst_view.overall: Sabah are 31st of 36 with 3 points and Barcelona 5th with 9, so Barcelona need the win to stay in the top 8, while Sabah come in after a 5-1 league win at Sumgayit and Valdas Dambrauskas wants his side to compete in front of a big crowd at the Olympic Stadium in Baku. Barcelona landed on Monday after the longest European away trip in the club's history and rested on arrival; Lamine Yamal (right ankle) stayed in Barcelona along with the injured Rodri, Xavi Espart, Christensen, Hamza and Roony Bardghji, and the numbers already count Yamal, Rodri, Espart and Christensen. Reserve winger Jesse Bisiwu and centre-back Alex Campos travel, but the reports link that to Yamal's absence rather than wider rotation, so Raphinha, Pedri, Olmo, De Jong and Cubarsi are expected. Aden McCarthy's ban for Sabah is counted. Scottish referee Nick Walsh is in charge, and his high card rate (5.8 a game) is already in the numbers; nothing new since yesterday moves the view.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals (1.2 Sabah, 3.1 Barcelona), already taking off Lamine Yamal (-16.7%), who gives about a fifth of Barcelona's goal involvement, plus Rodri, Espart and Christensen, and counting both sides' good scoring runs. The travelling squad is otherwise near full strength with Raphinha, Olmo and Pedri, and the youngsters called up are cover rather than a sign of rotation, so I stay at 4.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 6.6 of them for Barcelona, who should have most of the ball against a deep Sabah block. Without Yamal, Barcelona's width comes from Raphinha, Adeyemi or Gordon, which still pushes play to the flanks, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, already adding Nick Walsh's high card rate (+25.9%) and Sabah's busy recent card record (+10.9%), which fits a side chasing the ball for long spells, and taking a little off for Barcelona's quieter run (-5.2%). That is already a high figure for a game with no rivalry, and I found nothing beyond it, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots (8.9 Sabah, 25.6 Barcelona), already lifted for Barcelona's heavy recent shooting (+10.6%) and Sabah's (+4.3%). Yamal is a big source of Barcelona's shots, which the numbers only take off goals, but Sabah's confidence after a 5-1 win and a home crowd could open the game up; these pull both ways, so I stay at 34.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, already raised for Barcelona's sharp recent finishing (+8.5%) against a Sabah defence that has let plenty through. The long trip and Yamal's absence are small points against, Sabah's attacking intent points the other way, and there is no sign of rotation, so I stay at 12.3.
